title: Affine chart transitions without coherence
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative local ring and let $C$ be its maximal-ideal adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with structural homomorphism $\varphi:A\to C$. Let $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ be open, $q:Y\to U$ and $s:E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ morphisms of schemes, and $D$ a supplied overlap identification [def-sbc-punctured-completion-matching-sections]. Let $t\in\mathbb N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to A$, and suppose $D(f_i)\subseteq U$ and $V_i=(q\circ U.\iota)^{-1}D(f_i)$ is affine for every $i$. Put $O=Y\times_U(\operatorname{Spec}C|_U)$ and $p:O\to Y$ its projection. Assume also that $E$ is affine. There exist modules $M'$ over $C$ and $M_i$ over $A_{f_i}$, $A$-linear equivalences $\alpha_i:(M')_{f_i}\simeq C\otimes_A M_i$ and $\alpha_{ij}:(M_i)_{f_j}\simeq(M_j)_{f_i}$, with $\alpha_i$ commuting with the canonical localized $C$-action. These are the fields of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] except for square and cocycle; no coherence equation is assumed or asserted. There are a $C$-linear equivalence $e:M'\simeq\Gamma(E,\top)$ for its structural action and additive equivalences $c_i:M_i\simeq\Gamma(Y,V_i)$, $b_{ij}:(M_j)_{f_i}\simeq\Gamma(Y,V_i\cap V_j)$, $d_i:C\otimes_A M_i\simeq\Gamma(O,p^{-1}V_i)$. They satisfy $b_{ij}(\alpha_{ij}(m/1))=c_i(m)|_{V_i\cap V_j}$, $b_{ij}(n/1)=c_j(n)|_{V_i\cap V_j}$, $d_i(\alpha_i(m'/1))=D.\mathrm{toCompleted}^*(e(m'))|_{p^{-1}V_i}$, $d_i(1\otimes m)=p^*c_i(m)$, for all original elements. Moreover $b_{ij}(a m)$ is the structural image of $a\in A$ times $b_{ij}(m)$, and $d_i(z m)$ is the structural image of $z\in C$ times $d_i(m)$.

proof.text: let V_i be the inverse image of D(f_i) in Y. The hypotheses give affineness of E and every V_i. Set M'=Gamma(E,top) with the structural C-action, and M_i=Gamma(Y,V_i). The structural A-action on M_i extends uniquely to A_(f_i), since f_i is invertible on V_i. Thus e and c_i are identity identifications of these actual section rings, not arbitrary witnesses. The basic-open section localization theorem identifies (M_j)_(f_i) with Gamma(Y,V_i intersect V_j), defining b_ij by its universal property. The affine pullback tensor-product description identifies C tensor_A M_i with Gamma(O,p inverse-image V_i), giving d_i. The given overlap isomorphism D, and its equation D.over, identify the same completed open with the principal open f_i of E. Its sections are (M')_(f_i). Compose these section equivalences to obtain alpha_i, and use the common double intersection to obtain alpha_ij. All maps commute with structural scalars, proving alpha_smul, b_scalar and d_scalar. The localization map m to m/1 becomes actual restriction of m, proving b_left, b_right and d_prime. The tensor map m to 1 tensor m is pullback of sections, proving d_chart. No square or cocycle is asserted here. Empty principal opens have the zero section ring and zero localized modules, so the same universal properties apply. For t=0 only M' and e are needed.
